column7: Pasta cooks fine in a microwave, in a big bowl with plenty of room: cover it with boiling water from the kettle, add a good pinch of salt, and give it 8 to 10 minutes on full power, stirring once at the halfway point so the pieces at the top get turned under. Use a bowl at least twice the size of the pasta, because it foams up over the edge otherwise. Test a piece at 8 minutes - it goes from chalky to mushy quickly - then drain it straight away.

column7: Beat two or three eggs with a pinch of salt and a splash of milk in a mug or a small bowl, add a small knob of butter, and cook on full power in 30-second bursts, stirring properly between each one. Two eggs take about 90 seconds to two minutes in total, and they should come out still slightly wet - they carry on setting as you stir, and a microwave takes them from soft to rubbery in twenty seconds. Salt again at the end, not before. A whole egg in its shell is the one thing to keep out: it bursts, so if you want a fried egg on a plate, break it and prick the yolk first.

column7: Put the veg in a microwave-safe bowl with two or three tablespoons of water, cover it with a plate or cling film with a corner turned back, and cook on full power: green beans and peas 3 to 4 minutes, broccoli and cauliflower florets 4 to 5, carrot batons 5 to 6, from raw. Stir or turn them over at halfway, and stand for a minute before you lift the cover, because the steam is hotter than boiling water. Stop while they are still bright and a knife goes in with a little resistance - they carry on cooking as they stand.

column7: The clock decides, not the look: two hours at room temperature is the limit, and one hour if the room is hot. Under that, box it and put it in the fridge and use it in the next day or two. Over it, bin anything with meat, fish, rice, dairy, eggs or a sauce, because the bugs that make you ill leave the taste and the smell alone and reheating does not undo it. Bread, cake, biscuits, jam and fruit are the exceptions and keep on the counter for days.

column7: Nothing fancy for the first day: a named bag with a pencil case (two pens, a pencil, a rubber, a ruler), a water bottle, a packed lunch or the money loaded on the dinner account, and the PE kit the school asked for, in a bag of its own if they can. Label everything, including the coat and the shoes, and put the timetable in the front pocket. Buy the cheap version of each until the school sends its list, then fill the gaps.
